classification.difficultyReason: Students must diagnose three defects without being told which features to inspect, connecting the taught numerical scale and stack conventions to unequal dot sizes, misalignment and the missing equally spaced value 5. This is routine diagnostic application at Development level.

content.prompt: What are three things wrong with this dot plot?

spec.description: Deliberately faulty dot plot. Three equal ticks labelled 3,4,6; three aligned markers over 3, five zigzag markers over 4, two larger markers over 6. Source turquoise mapped to blue; ordinary axis and labels black.
spec.mathematics: Preserve missing 5 and equal physical tick intervals despite unequal numerical increments. Preserve unequal marker sizes and horizontal offsets in the middle stack.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent intentionally defective question figure; no corrective annotations.

answer.short: Dots have different sizes; dots are not lined up; the number line is missing 5.
answer.worked: Use equal-sized dots and align repeated values in evenly spaced vertical stacks. Include every integer in the range: 3, 4, 5, 6, at equal intervals.
